context: The item is a refurbished phone with minor scratches.
transcript: Buyer ($60): I see this refurbished phone already has minor scratches, so let's skip the inflated pitch about how 'like new' it is. I'm offering $60 cash, so let me know if you want to make a real deal.

Seller ($190): At $60, you're practically taking food out of my family's mouth, especially when I already have two other buyers messaging me to pick it up tonight. Those cosmetic scratches don't affect the pristine screen at all, and I'm actually hesitant to part with it at a loss. I can reluctantly drop to $190, but you need to let me know right now before I give it to the next person.

Buyer ($85): Guilt trips and imaginary competing buyers won't cover up those scratches or justify a $190 price tag. Since you actually lowered your ask, I'll move up to $85, but you need to get realistic if you want a guaranteed sale today.

Seller ($175): $85 is an absolute insult to my family's hardship, especially when my phone is literally ringing right now with someone offering $180 for tomorrow. It hurts me deeply to do this, but if you can commit right this second to $175, I will reluctantly turn them away for a guaranteed deal today.

Buyer ($105): Spare me the sob story and the fake 'ringing phone'—if someone actually offered $180, you wouldn't be begging me to buy it for $175. However, since you dropped your price again, I'll raise my offer to $105. Take it or go sell to your imaginary buyer.

Seller ($160): It breaks my heart that you mock my situation, but I am so desperate to cover rent today that I'm forced to swallow my pride. I am literally shaking as I write this, but I'll make one last painful sacrifice and drop to $160 if you take it right now. Please don't kick me while I'm down—decide immediately before I give up and sell to the other buyer.

Buyer ($130): The dramatic shaking and rent sob stories won't work on me, but at least you made a real price drop to $160. Because of that reduction, I will increase my offer to $130 cash today. Take this guaranteed money right now or go test your theatrical skills on someone else.

Seller ($150): I can't believe you're forcing me to choose between basic survival and my self-respect, but my landlord is literally demanding rent this very second. I will make the ultimate, heartbreaking sacrifice and drop to $150 if you send the money right now. If you refuse, I am immediately handing the phone over to the buyer who just pulled up outside.
Buyer ($150): Nice try with the imaginary buyer pulling up outside, but since you finally came down to a reasonable price, we have a deal. I'll take it for $150 cash. <AGREEMENT>
